```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D

DOC = "PCR-004"
UO = "harvest"
UO_TITLE = "Harvest and Clarification (Step 4)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from config -> model -> outputs) ------------
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
p_cg = uo.param("centrifuge_g")
p_df = uo.param("depth_filter_load")
p_tb = uo.param("turbidity")


def _rng(edges, unit=""):
    """Range string from a [lo, hi] pair, matching the parameter tables."""
    tail = f" {unit}" if unit else ""
    return f"{edges[0]:g}–{edges[1]:g}{tail}"


def _width(edges):
    return float(edges[1]) - float(edges[0])


U_CG, U_DF, U_TB = "g", "L/m^2^", "NTU"
cg_par, cg_nor = _rng(p_cg.prange, U_CG), _rng(p_cg.nor, U_CG)
df_par, df_nor = _rng(p_df.prange, U_DF), _rng(p_df.nor, U_DF)
tb_par, tb_nor = _rng(p_tb.prange, U_TB), _rng(p_tb.nor, U_TB)
cg_sp = f"{p_cg.setpoint:g} {U_CG}"
df_sp = f"{p_df.setpoint:g} {U_DF}"
df_max = f"{p_df.prange[1]:g} {U_DF}"
df_nor_high = f"{p_df.nor[1]:g} {U_DF}"
cg_ratio = _width(p_cg.prange) / _width(p_cg.nor)
df_ratio = _width(p_df.prange) / _width(p_df.nor)
tb_ratio = _width(p_tb.prange) / _width(p_tb.nor)

# process context: the nominal commercial-scale simulation and the yield waterfall
_ps = csv("process_summary.csv")
_yw = csv("yield_waterfall.csv")
row_up = _ps[_ps.step == uo.step - 1].iloc[0]      # production bioreactor (Step 3)
row_h = _ps[_ps.step == uo.step].iloc[0]           # this step
row_pa = _ps[_ps.step == uo.step + 1].iloc[0]      # Protein A capture (Step 5)
yw_h = _yw[_yw.step == uo.step].iloc[0]

step_yield = yw_h.step_yield
yield_cv = uo.raw["yield"]["cv"]
mass_in_kg = row_up.product_mass_g / 1000.0
mass_out_kg = row_h.product_mass_g / 1000.0
mass_loss_kg = mass_in_kg - mass_out_kg
train_yield = _yw.cumulative_yield.iloc[-1]
loss_share = (1.0 - step_yield) / (1.0 - train_yield)
turb_nom = row_h.turbidity_ntu
feed_viability = row_up.final_viability_pct
feed_titer = row_up.titer_g_per_l

# impurity burden handed forward to Protein A capture
hcp_harvest = CFG.unit_op("bioreactor").raw["rsm"]["harvest_centre"]["hcp"]
hcp_pa_pool = row_pa.pool_hcp_ng_mg
hcp_pa_fold = hcp_harvest / hcp_pa_pool
_hcp_cap = cap[cap.key == "hcp"].iloc[0]
hcp_ds_mean, hcp_ds_limit, hcp_ds_cpk = _hcp_cap["mean"], _hcp_cap.acc_high, _hcp_cap.Cpk
dna_ds_cpk = cap[cap.key == "residual_dna"].iloc[0].Cpk

# analytical performance (campaign method register)
_meth = csv("dev_methods.csv").set_index("id")
turb_prec = _meth.loc["AMV-3015", "precision_pct"]
turb_loq = _meth.loc["AMV-3015", "loq"]

# deviations
_dev = dev_facts(DOC)
n_dev = len(_dev)
_lots = csv("dev_lots.csv").set_index("id")
lot_df_id = _dev[_dev.dev_id == "DEV-004-01"].lot.iloc[0]
lot_df_use = _lots.loc[lot_df_id, "used_in"]
turb_exc_over_nor = dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu - p_tb.nor[1]
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Harvest and clarification is the primary recovery step of the A-Mab drug-substance process.
It removes cells and cell debris from the production bioreactor broth by continuous
disk-stack centrifugation (SOP-2005), and it clarifies the centrate through a depth filter
train and a sterile filter (SOP-2006). The step forms no product-quality attribute and is
credited with no impurity clearance. What it delivers is product recovery and a consistent,
low-solids feed to Protein A capture (PCR-005).

The characterization was executed under PCP-004 in a qualified scale-down model, and it
follows the Stage 1 process-design expectations of the lifecycle approach [@fda2011] and the
enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 [@ichq8], with the A-Mab case study as the process
reference throughout [@amab2009]. Three parameters were characterized, each one at a
time over a range two to three times the width of its normal operating range. Centrifugation
and depth-filter loading are key process parameters and post-clarification turbidity is a
general process parameter, and the step carries no critical process parameter, because none
of its parameters is linked to a critical quality attribute.

In the nominal commercial-scale simulation the step recovered `{python} pct(step_yield)` of
the product presented to it, which is `{python} f"{mass_out_kg:.1f}"` kg of the
`{python} f"{mass_in_kg:.1f}"` kg leaving the bioreactor, and it accounts for
`{python} pct(loss_share)` of the total product loss across the drug-substance train.
Post-clarification turbidity at the set-point condition was `{python} f"{turb_nom:g}"` NTU,
in the middle of its normal operating range of `{python} tb_nor`. Both results were obtained
over the characterized ranges given in §7 and in a scale-down model, so they are bounded by
that model and by those ranges.

The clarified harvest carries about `{python} f"{hcp_harvest:,.0f}"` ng/mg host cell protein
(HCP) into capture. That burden is set by the culture and cleared by the purification train,
not by this step. Protein A capture alone reduces it `{python} f"{hcp_pa_fold:.0f}"`-fold
(PCR-005), and the drug substance meets its limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_limit:g}"` ng/mg
with a capability of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_cpk:.2f}"` (§8). Two deviations were recorded,
investigated and closed. Both were retained without altering a parameter classification or a
characterized range (§13). The step is ready for Stage 2 with the ranges given in §7,
and its outcome rolls up into PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose principal mechanism of action is
antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity, and it is produced by fed-batch mammalian
cell culture and purified by a platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral
inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small-virus retentive filtration and
ultrafiltration or diafiltration. The train and the role of each step are given in
@tbl-train. Harvest and clarification sits between the production bioreactor (PCR-003) and
capture, and it is the only step of the train that handles unclarified broth.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(process_steps_df())
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug-substance process train and the principal role of each step. {#tbl-train}")
```

The step operates in two stages. In the first, the whole broth is fed continuously to a
disk-stack centrifuge, which sediments cells and the larger debris and discharges them as a
solids stream. The centrate is then passed through a depth filter train, which removes the
fine solids that the centrifuge cannot sediment, and finally through a sterile filter into
the capture feed vessel, where solids removal is judged by the turbidity of the clarified
harvest measured by nephelometry.

The step forms no critical quality attribute and reduces none, because it has no
chromatographic, chemical or size-based mechanism that acts on the antibody, so the glycan,
charge-variant and aggregate attributes formed in the bioreactor (PCR-003) pass through it
unchanged.
Host cell protein and residual DNA enter it with the broth and leave it with the clarified
harvest. Their clearance is the work of the purification steps, and the credit for it is
given in PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008.

## Objectives

The objectives of this characterization were:

- (i) To confirm that the step forms and modifies no critical quality attribute over the
  ranges studied.
- (ii) To quantify product recovery and its variability at commercial-equivalent scale.
- (iii) To establish the ranges of centrifugation force and depth-filter loading over which
  clarification remains acceptable.
- (iv) To classify each parameter of the step under SOP-4001.
- (v) To define the in-process controls that assure a consistent feed to Protein A capture.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process-design activity in the lifecycle sense [@fda2011], and it is
reported here as part of the record supporting the Biologics License Application. The
development approach follows ICH Q8 and ICH Q11, and criticality is treated as a continuum
under ICH Q9 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. Attributes are not sorted into critical and
non-critical alone. They carry a level of criticality that reflects both the impact of the
attribute and the uncertainty in that impact, and the parameters of a step are classified
against the attributes they affect.

No viral-clearance claim is made for this step, so ICH Q5A is not applied here [@ichq5a],
and the cumulative viral-clearance claim for the drug substance rests on low-pH inactivation
(PCR-006), anion exchange (PCR-008) and small-virus retentive filtration (PCR-009), where it
is consolidated into the summary held in PCMR-001.

## Related documents

The risk basis for the scope of this study is RA-001, the paired protocol is PCP-004, the
transfer context is PTP-001, and the cross-references are listed in @tbl-related.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

Centrifugation followed by depth filtration is the established primary-recovery platform at
Novacyte Biologics, and it has been used without change for three previous humanized IgG1
products (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab). The mechanisms are physical and well understood. Solids
are removed in the centrifuge by sedimentation, so removal improves as relative centrifugal
force (rcf) rises and as feed flow falls. The depth filter removes the fine solids that
remain, by a combination of size exclusion and adsorption, and its capacity is expressed as
the volume filtered per unit of filter area (`{python} U_DF`). As that capacity is consumed, retained solids
begin to pass and the turbidity of the filtrate rises.

Two expectations follow from these mechanisms, and the study was designed to test them. The
first is that clarification performance depends on centrifugation force and on filter
loading, and that the loading limit is reached before the sedimentation limit at the
platform set-points. The second is that neither setting changes product quality, because
neither has a mechanism that acts on the antibody, and prior product experience supports
both expectations, as does the treatment of primary recovery in the A-Mab case study
[@amab2009]. That experience reduced the scope of this study to a univariate assessment of
three parameters.

The impurity burden entering capture is set upstream. Host cell protein and DNA are released
by the culture, and the burden rises with culture duration and with the fall in
end-of-culture viability that accompanies it. In the nominal batch the culture was harvested
at a viability of `{python} f"{feed_viability:.1f}"` % and a titre of
`{python} f"{feed_titer:.2f}"` g/L. Clarification carries that burden forward, and it
neither adds to it nor reduces it.

## Quality attributes in scope

This step sets no critical quality attribute. The attributes it carries forward, and against
which its parameters were assessed, are given in @tbl-cqa. Host cell protein is the most
consequential of the three, at moderate to high criticality, because it is the impurity
present in the largest amount in the clarified harvest. Aggregate is of high criticality and
is the one attribute with a plausible mechanism at this step, since shear at the centrifuge
feed zone could in principle raise it. Residual DNA is of very low criticality on its own,
and is cleared by a large margin downstream.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["hcp", "aggregates_hmw", "residual_dna"]))
print()
print(": Quality attributes carried forward by the step, with acceptance criteria and "
      "criticality. None is formed or cleared here. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 ranked every parameter of the step for potential impact on quality attributes and for
potential interaction with other parameters, and all three fell into the band for which a
univariate assessment is sufficient, with none reaching the band that warrants a
multivariate design. The reason is the same in each case. No parameter of the step has a
mechanism by which it can act on a quality attribute, so the risk it carries is a
process-performance risk and not a quality risk.

The characterized ranges were widened beyond the routine control ranges so that the study
would describe process robustness and not only the target condition. Centrifugation was
studied over `{python} cg_par`, which is `{python} f"{cg_ratio:.0f}"` times the width of its
normal operating range, and depth-filter loading over `{python} df_par` and turbidity over
`{python} tb_par`, each about `{python} f"{df_ratio:.0f}"` times the width of the
corresponding normal operating range. The lower centrifugation edge was set where prior
platform data show that sedimentation becomes incomplete, and the upper depth-filter edge
was set at the loading beyond which the platform filter is no longer guaranteed by its
vendor.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

A scale-down model of the harvest and clarification step was qualified against
commercial-scale data before the study, under SOP-1001. The centrifuge model is a bench
disk-stack machine operated at the same relative centrifugal force and at a feed flow scaled
to hold the equivalent settling area constant (the sigma factor), so that the sedimentation
duty of the commercial machine (SOP-2005) is reproduced. The depth filter train uses the same filter
media as the commercial train and is operated at the same loading in litres per square
metre, so that capacity translates directly.

Qualification compared step yield and post-clarification turbidity between the model and the
commercial-scale process at the target condition, and found no difference that the
analytical methods could resolve. The qualification record is held under SOP-1001 and is not
reproduced here. Two limits of the model should be read together with its results. It
reproduces the sedimentation and capacity duties, but it does not reproduce the full shear
history of a commercial disk-stack machine, and it operates at hold times shorter than those
of a commercial harvest. Both limits are addressed by confirming yield and turbidity at
scale during process performance qualification.

## Operation

The step was operated under SOP-2005 for centrifugation and SOP-2006 for depth and sterile
filtration, harvest begins at the end of the production culture, and the whole broth is fed
to the centrifuge without a hold. The centrate is clarified immediately, and the clarified
harvest is held in the capture feed vessel until Protein A processing begins. Filter media
are flushed and integrity-tested before use under SOP-2006.

Inputs that are controlled to platform specification were not characterized here. Filter
media, buffers and the sterile filter are qualified by identity and quality on receipt, and
their control is exercised through the material specifications and not through a
characterization range.

## Analytical methods

Turbidity is the primary in-process measure of clarification and was determined by
nephelometry (AMV-3015), while host cell protein was measured by ELISA (AMV-3012) and
residual DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014), both to describe the burden handed to capture. Aggregate
was followed by SEC-HPLC (AMV-3011) to confirm that clarification does not change the size
distribution. The controlled documents that govern the step are listed in @tbl-methods, and
method performance is given in Appendix B.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=HARVEST_SOP_REFS, amvs=HARVEST_AMV_REFS))
print()
print(": Procedures and validated analytical methods applied to the step. {#tbl-methods}")
```

## Sampling plan

Each run was sampled at three points: the whole broth at the start of harvest, the centrate
once the centrifuge had reached steady discharge, and the clarified harvest at the end of
filtration. Turbidity was measured in-process on the clarified harvest and the remaining
assays were run on the end-of-filtration sample, and retained samples of every clarified
harvest are held for the campaign, so that a later question about a run can be answered on
retained material.

## Statistical methods

Each parameter was varied one at a time across its characterized range with the other
parameters held at their set-points. Responses were summarized descriptively, and no
multivariate model was fitted. That choice follows from the risk assessment. A response
surface is the predictive model that defines a design space, and it is worth building only
where a parameter acts on a quality attribute, which at this step is true of none of them,
so there is no response to model and no design space to define.

Commercial-scale capability for the attributes this step hands forward was taken from the
Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches that supports the
whole train, and it is reported in §8 as cross-step context. Capability is expressed as a
one-sided Cpk against the acceptance limit.

# Study design

## Parameters, ranges and the knowledge space

The parameters, their set-points, their normal operating ranges and the ranges over which
they were characterized are given in @tbl-params, together with the final classification and
the study type. The characterized range is the knowledge space of the step. It is wider than
the normal operating range on both sides, and the normal operating range is nested inside it
with margin at each edge.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
print()
print(": Parameters of the harvest and clarification step, with set-points, normal "
      "operating ranges, characterized ranges, final classification and study type. "
      "{#tbl-params}")
```

Post-clarification turbidity appears in the register as a parameter, but it behaves as an
outcome and is not set by the operator. It is the measured result of the centrifugation and
filtration settings and the attribute by which the clarified harvest is accepted for
capture, and it is characterized and controlled as a range for that reason.

## Univariate assessment

No designed experiment was executed at this step, and none is reported. Centrifugation force
was assessed across `{python} cg_par` with depth-filter loading at its set-point of
`{python} df_sp`. Depth-filter loading was then assessed across `{python} df_par` with
centrifugation at its set-point of `{python} cg_sp`, and turbidity was recorded on every
run, with product quality measured on the clarified harvest of each. Verification runs at
the set-point condition bracketed the study, so that a drift in the model or in the assays
over the campaign would have been visible.

The limitation of a univariate design is that it cannot resolve an interaction between the
two settings. That limitation is accepted here because the two act on different solids
populations, the centrifuge on the sedimentable fraction and the filter on the fine
fraction, and because neither acts on product quality. An interaction between them could
change clarification performance, and it could not change a quality attribute.

# Results

## Step yield and mass balance

The step recovers almost all of the product presented to it. In the nominal commercial-scale
simulation `{python} f"{mass_in_kg:.1f}"` kg of A-Mab entered the centrifuge and
`{python} f"{mass_out_kg:.1f}"` kg left the sterile filter, a step yield of
`{python} pct(step_yield)`. The loss of `{python} f"{mass_loss_kg:.1f}"` kg is product held
in the discharged solids and in the wetted filter train. Step yield varies from batch to
batch with a coefficient of variation of `{python} pct(yield_cv)`.

Recovery showed no dependence on centrifugation force or on depth-filter loading over the
ranges assessed, and the loss is dominated by hold-up in the solids and in the filter media,
which does not change appreciably across those ranges. The step accounts for
`{python} pct(loss_share)` of the total product loss across the train, which delivers a
cumulative yield of `{python} pct(train_yield)` (@fig-yield), and yield at this step is
therefore a process-performance concern and not a constraint on the process.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print("![Cumulative product yield across the drug-substance train, with harvest and "
      "clarification as the first loss in the sequence."
      "](../outputs/figures/fig_yield_waterfall.png){#fig-yield}")
```

## Clarification performance and filter capacity

Clarification met its in-process expectation across the ranges studied, with one excursion
that is described below. Post-clarification turbidity at the set-point condition was
`{python} f"{turb_nom:g}"` NTU, in the middle of the normal operating range of
`{python} tb_nor`. The nephelometric method has a precision of `{python} f"{turb_prec:g}"` %
and a limit of quantitation of `{python} f"{turb_loq:g}"` NTU (Appendix B), so the excursion
described below is well outside assay variability.

Turbidity rose as depth-filter loading approached the top of its characterized range, which
is the expected consequence of consuming filter capacity and is the mechanism set out in
§2.1. One run exceeded the upper limit of the normal operating range and reached
`{python} f"{dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu:g}"` NTU, which is
`{python} f"{turb_exc_over_nor:g}"` NTU above that limit, at a loading near the maximum
characterized value of `{python} df_max` (DEV-004-02, §13). The value remains inside the
characterized turbidity range of `{python} tb_par`, and the run was retained.
Centrifugation force produced no comparable trend over `{python} cg_par`, which is
consistent with sedimentation being complete well below the upper edge of that range.

## Impurity burden carried to Protein A capture

The clarified harvest carries a large host cell protein burden into capture. At the nominal
culture condition the level is about `{python} f"{hcp_harvest:,.0f}"` ng/mg by ELISA, and
residual DNA is present at a correspondingly high level. Neither is reduced here. Both are
carried forward to Protein A capture, which is the first step of the train with a mechanism
that separates them from the antibody (affinity binding).

Clearance is a property of the purification train and not of this step. Protein A capture
reduces host cell protein `{python} f"{hcp_pa_fold:.0f}"`-fold, to
`{python} f"{hcp_pa_pool:,.0f}"` ng/mg in the capture pool (PCR-005). Cation exchange and
anion exchange then complete the reduction (PCR-007, PCR-008), and the drug substance meets
its host cell protein limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_limit:g}"` ng/mg with a mean of
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_mean:.1f}"` ng/mg (§8). The contribution of harvest and clarification to
that outcome is the consistency of the material it hands over, not a log of clearance.

## Product quality across the step

No quality attribute changed across clarification, and aggregate, charge-variant and glycan
levels measured in the clarified harvest were the same as those in the bioreactor broth
within the variability of the methods, which is what a step with no mechanism to act on the
antibody should give. Aggregate was followed most closely, by SEC-HPLC, because shear at the
centrifuge feed zone is the one plausible product-quality risk here. No increase was seen
over the centrifugation range assessed.

That null result is a finding, and it is retained in the knowledge space. It is the evidence
that supports classifying both settable parameters as key and not critical (§9), and it is
the reason the step contributes nothing to the design space of the drug substance (§6). The
result is bounded by the ranges in @tbl-params, by the scale-down model described in §3.1,
and by the single culture condition from which the harvest material was taken.

# Design space

This step contributes no design space, since a design space is the multivariate region of
parameter settings that is known to give acceptable values of the critical quality
attributes, and it can only be defined for a step whose parameters act on such an attribute.
Harvest and clarification has no parameter that does, so the region is empty and its
parameters are controlled as ranges instead, and the A-Mab case study reaches the same
conclusion for the steps of the process that do not affect product quality [@amab2009].

Two consequences follow. Movement of centrifugation force or depth-filter loading within the
ranges given in §7 is not a change to the design space of the drug substance, and it is
managed under the quality system as a process-performance matter [@ichq10]. Operation
outside those ranges is a change, and it requires the assessment set out in the control
strategy, since the ranges themselves are bounded by the scale-down model and by the single
culture condition studied.

# Proven acceptable ranges

Each parameter was assessed univariately over its characterized range, and each range is
proven acceptable over its full width for the process-performance criteria of the step. The
ranges are given in @tbl-par. The acceptance basis here is not a drug-substance
specification, because the step governs no attribute that carries one, and it is instead the
pair of in-process criteria that the step must meet, which are the recovery of the product
and the delivery of a clarified harvest fit for capture.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_par = report_params(UO).rename(columns={"Char. range": "Proven acceptable range"})
show(_par[["Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Proven acceptable range", "Class"]])
print()
print(": Proven acceptable ranges for the harvest and clarification parameters. The proven "
      "acceptable range is the univariately characterized range in each case. {#tbl-par}")
```

Centrifugation is proven acceptable over `{python} cg_par` and depth-filter loading over
`{python} df_par`, and the normal operating ranges of `{python} cg_nor` and
`{python} df_nor` sit inside those ranges with margin at both edges. Turbidity is proven
over `{python} tb_par` in the sense that clarified harvest across that range was acceptable
to capture, but it is controlled to `{python} tb_nor` because the upper part of the wider
range is only reached when filter capacity is nearly exhausted. The worst case that the
ranges must satisfy is therefore the high-loading corner, where filter capacity is most
nearly consumed and turbidity is highest.

These are univariate ranges and not a multivariate region. They were established with the
other parameters at their set-points, so they carry the limitation set out in §4.2.
They are bounded by the scale-down model, by the ranges studied, and by the culture
condition from which the harvest material came.

# Process capability and robustness

The step has no process capability of its own to report, because it governs no quality
attribute and therefore has no acceptance limit to be capable against. The capability that
its output eventually supports is given in @tbl-cap for the two impurities it hands forward,
and both figures are commercial-scale results from the Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches that belongs to the purification train.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(["hcp", "residual_dna"]), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Commercial-scale capability for the impurities carried forward by this step. The "
      "clearance credit belongs to PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008. {#tbl-cap}")
```

Host cell protein reaches a mean of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_mean:.1f}"` ng/mg against a limit of
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_limit:g}"` ng/mg, a capability of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_cpk:.2f}"`, and
residual DNA is capable by a wider margin at `{python} f"{dna_ds_cpk:.2f}"`. Neither margin
is earned here, and this report claims none of it. What this step contributes is a feed of
consistent solids content and consistent impurity burden (turbidity and HCP), which is the
condition under which the capture step performs as characterized in PCR-005.

The robustness of the step is expressed in its own terms. Step yield varies with a
coefficient of variation of `{python} pct(yield_cv)`, and clarification held within its
normal operating range on every run but one over the loading and centrifugation ranges
studied. That robustness statement is bounded by the normal operating ranges in
@tbl-params, by the scale-down model of §3.1, and by the analytical precision given in
Appendix B.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified under SOP-4001 from the demonstrated effects and from the risk
of operating outside its range. The classifications are given in @tbl-params, and the reason
for each is as follows.

- Centrifugation force is a key process parameter. It governs solids removal and therefore
  the load presented to the depth filter, and no effect on any quality attribute was seen
  across `{python} cg_par`.
- Depth-filter loading is a key process parameter. It governs filter capacity and
  post-clarification turbidity, and it is readily controlled by fixing the filter area to
  the batch volume, so the risk of leaving its range is low.
- Post-clarification turbidity is a general process parameter. It is an outcome of the two
  settings above, it has no demonstrated link to a quality attribute, and it is monitored as
  the acceptance measure for the feed to capture.

The step carries no critical process parameter and no well-controlled critical process
parameter, and of the `{python} f"{V['n_cpp']:g}"` quality-linked parameters in the
drug-substance control strategy none belongs to this step. The absence of an effect is not a
gap in the study, and it is the evidence, gathered over ranges two to three times the width
of the routine control ranges, that supports the classification above.

# Contribution to the control strategy

The step contributes four elements to the control strategy of the drug substance. First,
centrifugation force and depth-filter loading are held within the normal operating ranges of
@tbl-params, which assures recovery and clarification. Second, post-clarification turbidity
is monitored in-process on every batch (AMV-3015), with the upper limit of its normal
operating range as the alert level and the upper edge of the characterized range as the action level. Third,
depth filter media are flushed and integrity-tested before use under SOP-2006, with the
flush volume set by the deviation described in §13.1. Fourth, the clarified harvest is
accepted for capture against turbidity, which is the feed-consistency link to PCR-005.

Three things the step does not do should be equally clear. It clears no host cell protein
and no DNA, so no clearance credit is taken for it anywhere in the package. It takes no viral-clearance credit, and the cumulative claim rests on PCR-006,
PCR-008 and PCR-009. It forms no quality attribute, so it imposes no constraint on the
design space of the drug substance. The contributions above roll up into the overall control
strategy in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The step is well understood, and the understanding is simpler than that of any other step in
the train. Its parameters act on solids and on recovery. They do not act on the antibody,
and the study found nothing that qualifies that statement over ranges two to three times the
width of the routine control ranges. The practical consequence is that the control strategy
for this step is a process-performance control strategy, and no parameter of it needs the
control that a critical process parameter would require.

The scale-down model is fit for the claims made from it. It reproduces the sedimentation
duty of the commercial centrifuge and the loading duty of the commercial filter train, and
qualification found no difference in yield or turbidity at the target condition. It does
not reproduce the full shear history of the commercial machine and it operates at shorter
hold times, but neither limit undermines the conclusions, because those conclusions concern
recovery and solids removal and not a shear-sensitive attribute. Both are closed at scale
during process performance qualification (PPQ).

Two deviations were recorded, and neither changed a conclusion. The more consequential of
the two was a turbidity excursion to `{python} f"{dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu:g}"` NTU on a
run loaded near the top of the characterized range. It was retained because the value stayed
inside the characterized range and the root cause is the known capacity mechanism. The other
deviation was a pre-use flush turbidity above its alert level, which was resolved by
extending the flush before the filter was used. The details of both are in §13.

Three limitations should be carried forward. The univariate design cannot resolve an
interaction between centrifugation and filter loading, which is accepted because neither
acts on quality (§4.2). The characterization used harvest material from a
single culture condition, so a change to the culture that materially altered the solids load
would warrant a reassessment of filter capacity. Turbidity is an indirect measure of solids,
and it does not distinguish a small quantity of large particles from a large quantity of
fine ones.

# Conclusions

Harvest and clarification is characterized and ready for Stage 2. The step forms no critical
quality attribute and changes none, and its parameters were shown to have no effect on
product quality over ranges two to three times the width of the routine control ranges. It
recovers `{python} pct(step_yield)` of the product presented to it and delivers a clarified
harvest at `{python} f"{turb_nom:g}"` NTU at the set-point condition.

Centrifugation force and depth-filter loading are key process parameters and
post-clarification turbidity is a general process parameter, so the step carries no critical
process parameter and it contributes no design space. The proven acceptable ranges of §7 are
the characterized ranges, and they are bounded by the scale-down model and by the single
culture condition studied. The impurity burden the step hands forward is cleared downstream,
where host cell protein reaches a capability of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_cpk:.2f}"` against its
limit. Two deviations were recorded, and both were retained without effect on the
classifications or the ranges. The outcome rolls up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan {#sec-deviations}

`{python} f"{n_dev:g}"` deviations from PCP-004 were recorded during execution, and each was
investigated, root-caused and impact-assessed before the study was closed. Neither altered a
parameter classification, a characterized range or a conclusion of this report. The register
is given in @tbl-dev, and each deviation is described below.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Register of deviations recorded during execution of PCP-004. {#tbl-dev}")
```

## DEV-004-01 — pre-use flush turbidity above alert

The pre-use flush of a depth filter lot gave a turbidity of
`{python} f"{dev_004_01_flush_turbidity_ntu:g}"` NTU (AMV-3015), above the alert level
applied to flush water, and the lot was `{python} lot_df_id`, allocated to
`{python} lot_df_use`. A filter
that sheds media fines into the flush could carry those fines into the clarified harvest,
which is why the alert exists.

The investigation compared the flush record with the volume specified in SOP-2006 and found
that the initial flush volume applied was below it, and extending the flush brought the
turbidity down, so that the filter was used only after the flush met its specification. The
root cause is an insufficient initial flush volume and not a defect in the media, and the
lot was released for use and the run was retained. The flush volume specified in SOP-2006
has been made an explicit step of the batch record, which is the control now carried into
the control strategy (§10).

## DEV-004-02 — post-clarification turbidity excursion

Post-clarification turbidity on one run reached
`{python} f"{dev_004_02_turbidity_max_ntu:g}"` NTU, which is
`{python} f"{turb_exc_over_nor:g}"` NTU above the upper limit of the normal operating range
of `{python} tb_nor`. The excursion was detected by in-process turbidity monitoring under
AMV-3015 during the run, and the clarified harvest of that run was quarantined pending
assessment.

The investigation established that the run was loaded to near the maximum of the
characterized depth-filter range, at which capacity is nearly consumed, and that is the
capacity mechanism described in §2.1, with the excursion its expected consequence at the
edge of the range. The value stayed inside the characterized turbidity range of
`{python} tb_par`, and it is well outside the `{python} f"{turb_prec:g}"` % precision of the
method, so it is a real effect and not assay noise. Product quality on that run was within
the same variability as the rest of the study.

The run was retained and its data were used, and the disposition rests on two findings. The
excursion occurred outside the normal operating range of depth-filter loading, so it does
not describe routine operation, and the material remained acceptable for capture. The
control that follows is the upper limit of `{python} df_nor_high` on loading, which is
already the normal operating limit and is now supported by direct evidence of what happens
above it.
